title: Exponential-Size Circuit Complexity is Comeager in Symmetric Exponential Time

                               Exponential-Size Circuit Complexity is

                                                              Abstract
                                                                                                                n
            Lutz (1987) introduced resource-bounded category and showed the circuit size class SIZE( 2n ) is meager
       within ESPACE. Li (2024) established that the symmetric alternation class SE2 contains problems requiring circuits
                 n
       of size 2n .
            In this note, we extend resource-bounded category to SE2 by defining meagerness relative to single-valued FSP2
       strategies in the Banach-Mazur game. We show that Li’s FSP2 algorithm for the Range Avoidance problem yields
                                                n
       a winning strategy, proving that SIZE( 2n ) is meager in SE2 .
            Consequently, languages requiring exponential-size circuits are comeager in SE2 : they are typical with respect
       to resource-bounded category.


1    Introduction
Resource-bounded category, introduced by Lutz [14–16], provides a way to analyze the typical properties of com-
                                                                                     n
plexity classes using topological notions of size. Lutz showed that the class SIZE( 2n ) of languages decidable by
                  n
circuits of size 2n is meager within the exponential-space class ESPACE.
                                           n
Theorem 1.1. (Lutz [14–16]) SIZE( 2n ) is meager in ESPACE.
   The symmetric exponential-time class SE2 is an exponential version of the class SP2 [5, 21] and it lies between E
and ESPACE. Building on work by Korten [12] and Chen, Hirahara, and Ren [6], Li [13] recently proved that SE2
contains languages that require near-maximum circuit size.
                                           n
Theorem 1.2. (Li [13]) SE2 ̸⊆ SIZE( 2n ).
    This solved a longstanding open problem to show the second level of the exponential-time hierarchy requires
exponential-size circuits [1–3, 9, 10, 19, 20]. Li’s proof technique involves constructing a hard language using a
single-valued FSP2 algorithm (a function problem analogue of SP2 ). Given these developments, a natural question is
whether the category framework can be refined to operate within SE2 . Can we show that languages requiring large
circuits are not just present, but are in fact typical within SE2 ?
    In this note, we answer this question affirmatively. We adapt the resource-bounded category machinery to the
class SE2 by defining meagerness relative to single-valued FSP2 -computable constructors in the Banach-Mazur game.
Our main result shows that, analogous to Lutz’s result for ESPACE, small circuits are atypical within SE2 .
                          n
Theorem 1.3. SIZE( 2n ) is meager in SE2 .
    We prove this by demonstrating that Li’s single-valued FSP2 algorithm for the range avoidance problem [6, 12]
                                              n
provides a winning strategy against SIZE( 2n ) in the appropriate Banach-Mazur game. Thus, languages requiring
exponential-size circuits are not just present in SE2 —they are typical in the sense of resource-bounded category: the
class of such languages is comeager in SE2 .
    This paper is organized as follows. We present preliminaries on resource-bounded category and symmetric
alternation in Section 2. Our results are in Section 3. We conclude in Section 4 with an open question about
extending our results to resource-bounded measure.

2      Preliminaries
2.1     Resource-Bounded Category
Resource-bounded category was introduced by Lutz [14–16]. The Cantor space C is the set of all infinite binary
sequences. A language (or decision problem) is a subset of {0, 1}∗ . We identify each language with the element of
Cantor space that is its characteristic sequence according to the standard enumeration s0 = λ, s1 = 0, s2 = 1, s3 =
00, . . . of {0, 1}∗ . In this way, complexity classes (sets of languages) are viewed as subsets of Cantor space.
    Baire category classifies sets into two types: first category and second category. First category sets are also
commonly called meager. A set is meager if it is a countable union of nowhere dense sets. An equivalent definition
comes from Banach-Mazur games using functions called constructors.

Definition 2.1. A constructor is a total, single-valued function δ : {0, 1}∗ → {0, 1}∗ which satisfies x ⊏ δ(x) for
                                                                                                        ̸=

all x ∈ {0, 1} . The result of a constructor is the unique sequence R(δ) ∈ C that extends δ (λ) for all n.

    Let X ⊆ C and let ΓI and ΓII be two classes of functions. In the Banach-Mazur game G[X; ΓI , ΓII ] there are
two players I and II. A strategy in the game is a constructor. In a play of the game, player I chooses a strategy γ ∈ ΓI
and player II chooses a strategy δ ∈ ΓII . The result of this play is the sequence R(γ, δ) = R(δ ◦ γ). Intuitively, the
result is the sequence obtained when the two players start with the empty string and take turns extending it with their
strategies. A winning strategy for player II is a strategy δ ∈ ΓII such that for every γ ∈ ΓI , R(γ, δ) ̸∈ X.

Theorem 2.2. (Banach and Mazur) A class X ⊆ C is meager if and only if player II has a winning strategy in the
game G[X; all, all].

      In resource-bounded category, ∆ denotes a resource bound [16, 17]. Examples of ∆ include:

                                    all = {f | f : {0, 1}∗ → {0, 1}∗ }
                                     p = {f | f is polynomial-time computable}
                               pspace = {f | f is polynomial-space computable}

For a resource bound ∆, we define the result class

                                      R(∆) = {R(δ) | δ ∈ ∆ is a constructor}.

Then R(all) = C, R(p) = E, and R(pspace) = ESPACE [16]. Resource-bounded category [16] is defined by
requiring player II’s winning strategy to be computable within a resource bound ∆.

Definition 2.3. Let X ⊆ C and let ∆ be a resource bound.

    1. X is ∆-meager if player II has a winning strategy in the game G[X; all, ∆].

    2. X is ∆-comeager if X c is ∆-meager.

    3. X is meager in R(∆) if X ∩ R(∆) is ∆-meager.

    4. X is comeager in R(∆) if X c is meager in R(∆).

The resource-bounded Baire category theorem [16] tells us that R(∆) is not ∆-meager.

    Another corollary is meagerness of SIZE( 2n ) in ENP under a derandomization hypothesis. This is because stan-
dard derandomization hypotheses [11] collapse FSP2 to FPNP via derandomization of FZPPNP . Resource-bounded
category in ENP is defined analogously to category in E, using polynomial-time constructors that have access to an
NP oracle in Definition 2.3.
Lemma 3.4. R(FPNP ) = ENP .

   1. X is FPNP -meager if player II has a winning strategy in the game G[X; all, FPNP ].

   2. X is meager in ENP if X ∩ ENP is FPNP -meager.

Corollary 3.5. If ENP requires 2Ω(n) -size NP-oracle circuits, then SIZE( 2n ) is meager in ENP .

Proof. Cai [4] showed that SP2 ⊆ ZPPNP . It also holds that single-valued FSP2 is contained in single-valued FZPPNP
[6]. Under the hypothesis, techniques of Klivans and van Melkebeek [11] derandomize FZPPNP to FPNP [6]. Thus

4    Conclusion
Lutz and Mayordomo [18] asked if P/poly has measure 0 in a class smaller than ∆E3 , the third level of the exponential-
time hierarchy. Theorem 1.3 implies P/poly is meager in SE2 . Resource-bounded measure may also be defined in SE2
using single-valued FSP2 martingales. Does P/poly have measure 0 in SE2 ?
